paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: a quarrel left to grow can swallow a lot of people. Ephraim asked why they weren't called, and then they threatened, "We will burn your house down with you inside!" (Judges 12:1). Jephthah answered that he did call, and that they did not save him (Judges 12:2). I think this was a moment for both sides to stop and talk, and instead it just kept climbing.

By the end, 42,000 Ephraimites were dead (Judges 12:6), and I won't joke about that one. Look at what Jephthah said just before the fighting: "the LORD delivered them into my hand" (Judges 12:3). A few verses later, the sword was pointed at Ephraim. I think that's worth sitting with, because winning one battle doesn't mean you'll handle the next fight well.

Then Ibzan, Elon and Abdon come and go, and each one ends the same way: died and buried (Judges 12:10, 12, 15). Leaders pass, but the way we treat people who hurt us is something we carry into every room. So when somebody leaves you out of the group chat, take a breath before you type. A hurt feeling is a lot easier to fix on day one than on day forty.
